habits.title: Add a second layer to sign-in
habits.detail: Enable passkeys or multifactor authentication on email, banking and important accounts. Prefer phishing-resistant options when available.

habits.title: Use unique passwords
habits.detail: Use a trusted password manager. Replace passwords reused across accounts.

habits.title: Keep software up to date
habits.detail: Turn on automatic updates for your phone, computer, browser and trusted security software.

habits.title: Make recovery possible
habits.detail: Keep a separate backup of important files and check that you can restore one.

habits.title: Verify unexpected requests
habits.detail: Use a known phone number or an app you already trust before sharing information or changing payments.

habits.title: Check account recovery options
habits.detail: Keep recovery details current and store backup sign-in codes somewhere secure. Do not paste them here.

habits.title: Review signed-in devices
habits.detail: Check important accounts for unfamiliar sessions and security alerts using their official settings.

habits.title: Check device security
habits.detail: Use the security settings and trusted protection software supplied or recommended by your device provider.

habits.title: Separate administrator access
habits.detail: Give staff only the access they need. Use a separate administrator account for privileged work.

habits.title: Give staff a reporting path
habits.detail: Make it easy to report suspicious messages and regularly practice spotting unusual requests.

habits.title: Verify payment changes by callback
habits.detail: Confirm new bank details or payment instructions with a known contact using a previously trusted number.

habits.title: Write a recovery plan
habits.detail: List your IT, bank and key provider contacts, recovery responsibilities and backup restoration steps.

incidents.title: I clicked a suspicious link
incidents.description: Take the next step based on what happened.

incidents.title: I shared a password or code
incidents.description: Recover access and review active sessions.

incidents.title: I sent money or payment details
My device shows a warning
incidents.description: Handle pop-ups, remote access or possible ransomware.

result.title: Email check
result.summary: Pause and verify this request through a trusted channel.

findings.title: Misleading text before the destination
findings.detail: A link includes an @ section. Text before @ is not the destination website.

findings.title: A request for sign-in secrets
findings.detail: The text appears to request a password, recovery phrase or sign-in code. Verify independently and do not share these secrets.

findings.title: Pressure to act quickly
findings.detail: Urgency can discourage checking a request. Take time to contact the sender through a trusted channel.

actions.title: Pause before responding
actions.detail: Do not use the message’s links, attachments or contact details until you verify the request independently.

actions.title: Use a trusted channel
actions.detail: Open the official app you already use or contact the organization using a number you already know is genuine.

actions.title: Keep and report the message
actions.detail: If it appears suspicious, use your email provider’s phishing report option or your organization’s IT reporting process. Keep evidence if money or access was lost.
